title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Lumina Partners
summary: Weekly co-sell pipeline review. Reviewed three priority deals (Acme Corp, NovaSys, Meridian Health). Discussed next milestones, joint demo scheduling, security ask list for Meridian, and pricing alignment for Acme. Action items assigned for joint pipeline doc and scheduling exec intro for Meridian. SE discussed performance/latency expectations and on-prem considerations for Meridian Health.
next_steps: Maya - circulate updated joint pipeline spreadsheet (link) by 2026-12-09
Ethan/Carlos - prepare performance notes and short benchmark plan for Meridian Health by 2026-12-13
Leah - schedule executive intro with Lumina/Sales + Redwood AE week of 12/13
Priya - confirm Acme pricing target and expected close date by 2026-12-10
Jared - share Meridian's SOC2/KMS checklist and contact for security review
action_items: Maya - share joint pipeline spreadsheet (https://redwood-internal.sheets/joint-pipeline) - due 2026-12-09
Carlos - draft short benchmark plan for Meridian (latency targets, model variants, hosted vs dedicated) - due 2026-12-13
Ethan - intro to Meridian security lead and provide customer SOC2 details - due 2026-12-10
Leah - coordinate exec intro and calendar invites - due 2026-12-11
Priya - confirm Acme commercial ask and pricing target - due 2026-12-10
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood on the AE side, with Carlos our SE and Leah from partnerships. How's everyone?
[00:06] Jared Cole: Hey Maya, good thanks. Jared here at Lumina. Priya and Ethan are on.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya. We're excited to run through the pipeline.
[00:14] Maya: Great. Agenda — quick pipeline rundown, call out blockers, security asks, and next steps. We'll start with Acme Corp. Priya, can you run that?
[00:23] Priya: Yeah. Acme is in late eval, they're asking for pricing alignment against a competitor — they mentioned Bedrock and Anthropic in the RFP. They're most sensitive to per-token cost and latency under 300ms for the main chat flow. They've asked for a joint demo next Thursday.
[00:36] Carlos Ramirez: Quick note on latency — 300ms is tight at 1k context unless we push dedicated capacity or aggressive batching. We can hit it for short turns on Hosted API with optimized model variants, but would recommend Redwood Dedicated for stable SLO at scale.
[00:49] Ethan Brooks: Do we have recent benchmarking numbers for the model they picked? They mentioned a Llama variant and sometimes the transcription mixes names.
[00:55] Carlos: We ran a 95th percentile test last month — for the quantized LLaMA-2-13b on A10s we saw ~220-350ms depending on seq length and KV cache hit rate. That's with lightweight prompt engineering and prefix caching. I'll share the exact sheet after.
[01:10] Priya: Okay that works; Acme is more interested in cost too. They asked our target ARR discount.
[01:15] Maya: On pricing, we should align. Priya, what's Lumina's commercial target?
[01:19] Priya: They want something under $Xk/month for pilot, scaling to committed next quarter. I can confirm exact number by Friday.
[01:25] Leah Chen: For the demo, we should propose a joint co-sell deck + short performance appendix. I'll take lead on the deck and Maya will do commercial.
[01:33] Maya: Sounds good. Next — NovaSys. Jared?
[01:36] Jared: NovaSys is an internal platform team; they're more about private deployment. They asked about VPC options and whether Redwood Private supports on-prem air-gapped deployments. They bring up KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:47] Carlos: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; for air-gapped we have a packaged on-prem option but we typically treat that as a separate engagement with longer lead times. There can be slight differences in autoscaling and the console feature set.
[02:00] Ethan: Any common blockers folks hit with Nova style customers?
[02:03] Carlos: Biggest are network egress and firewall rules plus cert rotation — we have a runbook for that. Also kernel selection nuances when customers require older GPUs. I might have miss-said kernel as 'car nel' earlier in notes.
[02:12] Priya: Okay good. We'll flag that in the technical checklist.
[02:16] Maya: Meridian Health is next — high priority. Jared, what's the status?
[02:20] Jared: Meridian's security team wants SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM confirmation, and a short benchmark running on their data pattern. They specifically asked if Redwood can guarantee data residency and a no-logs policy during eval.
[02:31] Maya: We can surface our SOC2 report and confirm KMS integrations; data residency is supported in region-specific Dedicated or Private deployments. For no-logs during eval, we'd need a signed MSA addendum; Leah can help coordinate.
[02:44] Leah: I can take the lead on the MSA addendum and intro to our legal. Jared, can you share Meridian's security contact?
[02:50] Jared: Yes — I'll drop the email in the pipeline sheet.
[02:53] Carlos: For the benchmark plan — quick thought: we'll run a 48-hour lightweight workload with typical message lengths, measure p95 latency and token cost. If they require on-prem, the scope changes; CPU/GPU types matter a lot.
[03:07] Ethan: Meridian is very strict — they said they'll want an HSM-backed KMS integration and in some cases FIPS validated hardware.
[03:13] Carlos: Noted. We'll call out HSM as a potential add-on and estimate extra time.
[03:18] Priya: Are we seeing any competitor motion specifically for Meridian?
[03:21] Jared: They had early calls with OpenAI for hosted, and another SI talking about building their own stack. Price and security are the key tradeoffs.
[03:28] Maya: Okay, that's the main pipeline. A couple cross-deal asks: 1) we need a single joint pipeline spreadsheet with expected close dates and key blockers, 2) Lumina requested an exec-level intro for Meridian, 3) we should align on discounts for Acme.
[03:42] Leah: I'll own the exec intro. I can propose Wed or Thu of 12/13 week.
[03:47] Priya: Wed works for most of our team.
[03:49] Maya: Great. On the joint pipeline sheet — I've put a starter version at https://redwood-internal.sheets/joint-pipeline. I'll update with the three deals and milestones.
[03:58] Carlos: One small technical note: for Acme's latency requirement, if they plan to use longer context windows we should plan for dedicated instances and possibly model quantization. There's a tradeoff in output quality; we'll doc expected quality delta.
[04:12] Priya: Are we comfortable sharing quantized model guidance in a public doc? Sometimes customers worry about hallucination differences.
[04:17] Carlos: We'll be transparent: show a few evals and where regression risk is. That's why we recommend a short A/B in pilot.
[04:25] Jared: For NovaSys, we need the runbook link and the cert rotation checklist — do you have that?
[04:31] Maya: Yes, Carlos will share a condensed runbook, and our infra docs link.
[04:36] Carlos: I'll upload the runbook and the recent perf sheet (note: sheet names sometimes get truncated in the auto transcript).
[04:43] Priya: Anything on legal procurement timelines? Acme indicated procurement will take three to four weeks after commercial terms.
[04:49] Leah: For Dedicated deals, typically procurement + infra onboarding is 4–6 weeks, but depends on security questions. Meridian could extend that.
[04:58] Maya: Ok, quick open items: pricing alignment for Acme, benchmark plan for Meridian, exec intro scheduling. Any other issues?
[05:06] Ethan: One ask from Meridian — they want a short non-prod demo that shows no data persistence during the eval. How do we usually demonstrate that?
[05:14] Carlos: We can show a configuration of ephemeral KV cache and a retention policy, and supply a signed demo plan. But as Maya said, legal needs a short addendum for no-logs.
[05:24] Jared: I'll get security contact and the SOC2 checklist in the sheet.
[05:28] Priya: I'll confirm Acme pricing target by Friday.
[05:31] Maya: Perfect. Leah, can you set the exec intro?
[05:34] Leah: Yup I'll send invites.
[05:36] Maya: Any competitor updates? Priya said Bedrock and Anthropic for Acme. We're also seeing OpenAI for Meridian. We should prepare a short win story comparing latency/cost and highlighting Redwood Console for traceability.
[05:48] Carlos: I'll prepare a 2-slide perf comparison and a note on cost per 1k tokens for the candidate models.
[05:55] Maya: Great. Last part — recap of action items. Maya to share joint pipeline by 12/09; Priya to confirm Acme pricing by 12/10; Jared to share Meridian security contact and checklist; Carlos/Ethan to draft benchmark plan by 12/13; Leah to schedule exec intro by 12/11.
[06:14] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:16] Jared: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:18] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the sheet and Slack. Bye.

Notes: transcript contains occasional minor mis-transcriptions (model names, kernel vs car nel) typical of automated notes. References to links are placeholders.
